clue.text: Learner I tick off and let out of detention

parts.note: taken as written
to tick someone off is to scold or reprimand them

explanation.surface: A teacher scolds a pupil and then releases them from an after-school detention.
explanation.definitionFit: To liberate someone is to free them, the same as releasing a prisoner from custody.

clue.text: Footballer's article in French paper given support

parts.note: le is the French for the
the FT is the Financial Times newspaper
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A newspaper in France runs a piece on a soccer player who is given backing.
explanation.definitionFit: A left-back is a defender who plays on the left side of a football team.

clue.text: What allows us to think of British bad weather

parts.note: rain is the weather nobody wants

explanation.surface: A wry question about what makes us reflect on Britain's gloomy climate.
explanation.definitionFit: The brain is the organ of the body responsible for thought.

clue.text: More dangerous run by one person sliding downhill

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
a skier slides down the slopes

explanation.surface: A run down the slopes by a lone skier becomes more hazardous.
explanation.definitionFit: Riskier is the comparative of risky, so it means more hazardous.

clue.text: Child hosts adult perfectly

indicators.note: the word for child hosts the letter, holding it inside

parts.note: a tot is a small child

explanation.surface: A youngster hosts a grown-up flawlessly.
explanation.definitionFit: To a T is an idiom meaning exactly or precisely right.

clue.text: Celeb with Mr Sheeran maybe gawked impolitely

parts.note: a celebrity is a star
Ed Sheeran, the singer, is one man called Ed

explanation.surface: A famous person out with Ed Sheeran was rudely ogled by onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: To stare is to look fixedly, which is rude when you gawp at someone.

clue.text: African's capital jaunt round Lima and India

parts.note: a trip is a short outing
O is round in shape
Lima is L in the NATO phonetic alphabet
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: A trip to the Peruvian capital and to India.
explanation.walkthrough: Lima and India look like a city and a country, but they are the radio code words for two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripoli is the capital city of Libya, a North African country.

clue.text: Revolutionary hairstyle for a swimmer

parts.note: a Red is a communist revolutionary
a mullet is a haircut short at the front and long at the back

explanation.surface: A rebel's radical haircut suits a person in the pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Red mullet is a fish, and fish are crossword swimmers.

clue.text: Object that's thrown in nightclub, almost, by American

indicators.note: almost all of the word is used, its final letter missing

parts.note: a disco is a dance club

explanation.surface: Something gets hurled across a nightclub by an American.
explanation.definitionFit: A discus is the heavy disc hurled by athletes in field events.

clue.text: Pole keeping standards up tires by Welsh river

parts.note: to flag is to tire or weaken
the Taff flows through Cardiff

explanation.surface: A post holding banners aloft wearies beside a river in Wales.
explanation.walkthrough: Standards here are flags, so the definition is a pole that holds flags up.
explanation.definitionFit: A flagstaff is the mast from which banners and ensigns are flown.

clue.text: Baffling material such as linoleum

definitions.meaning: second meaning: the covering laid on a floor

explanation.surface: A puzzling surface like lino.
explanation.definitionFit: Flooring is both the covering on a floor and the act of stumping someone completely.

clue.text: Banker's attempt to quit work

definitions.note: in crosswords a banker is a river, something with banks

indicators.note: the attempt leaves the word for work, so it is taken out

parts.note: industry means hard work or diligence
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: A financier gives up trying to do any work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Banker' reads as a city financier, but it is a river: something that has banks.
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of Pakistan, so it is a crossword banker.

clue.text: Desperado, some flipping recidivist I'd nabbed

indicators.note: the run of letters is flipped over and read backwards
only some of the letters of these words are used, a run spanning them

parts.note: the letters run across the end of recidivist, all of I'd and the start of nabbed

explanation.surface: A reoffender has been caught once again, an outlaw back in custody.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandit is an armed robber or outlaw, the same lawless figure as a desperado.

clue.text: Curtailed hot number by songstress in state capital

indicators.note: a curtailed word has its tail, the last letter, cut off

parts.note: taken as written before its tail is removed
Lulu is a Scottish pop singer famous since the 1960s

explanation.surface: A singer performs a sizzling song, shortened, in a state's chief city.
explanation.definitionFit: Honolulu is the capital city of the US state of Hawaii.

clue.text: Some cricket players, rather grey and gloomy

parts.note: an over is a set of six balls bowled in cricket, so a portion of the game
a cast is the set of actors in a play

explanation.surface: A few cricketers play on under a dull, dreary sky.
explanation.definitionFit: An overcast sky is clouded over, so the weather is dull and grey.

clue.text: Scorn Voltaire novel causing much debate

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters are put into a new order

parts.note: the thirteen letters of these two words are the ones rearranged

explanation.surface: Mocking a book by Voltaire stirs up an argument.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' looks like a book by the French writer, but it signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Something controversial provokes public argument and disagreement.

clue.text: Being poor, trainee dines simply, to an extent

indicators.note: only part of these words is used, a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the run starts in trainee, takes all of dines and the first letter of simply

explanation.surface: An apprentice short of money eats plain meals to some degree.
explanation.definitionFit: Neediness is the state of being in want, lacking money or necessities.

clue.text: Hard to hold on to, like a shoe worn in the house?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: slick or elusive in the grip

definitions.text: like a shoe worn in the house?
definitions.meaning: second meaning, playful: resembling a slipper, the soft indoor shoe

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the made-up sense: slipper plus a -y ending meaning 'like'.
explanation.definitionFit: Slippery describes something smooth and hard to grip, and whimsically something slipper-like.

clue.text: Green with envy, mostly, travelling in Montreal

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its last letter dropped

parts.note: taken as written before its last letter goes

indicators.note: letters that are travelling move about into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone touring Montreal is consumed by jealousy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green with envy' looks like one phrase, but only 'Green' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Green in the political sense means environmental, concerned with protecting nature.

clue.text: Queen admitted to V&A gallery

indicators.note: the letters are let inside the museum's letters

parts.note: the letters V, A and N from 'and' spell out the name
ER, Elizabeth Regina, stands for the Queen

explanation.surface: The monarch is let into the Victoria and Albert Museum in London.
explanation.walkthrough: The V&A is the Victoria and Albert Museum; read the ampersand as AND.
explanation.definitionFit: A veranda is a roofed porch along a house, also called a gallery in some regions.

clue.text: Son leaves most demanding, high peak

indicators.note: the son leaves, so that letter goes from the word

parts.note: severest means hardest or most exacting

explanation.surface: A son abandons the toughest climb, a lofty summit.
explanation.definitionFit: Everest is the world's tallest mountain, on the Nepal-Tibet border.

clue.text: Improved ale tucked into by non-drinker

indicators.note: the drink is tucked into, holding the non-drinker inside it

parts.note: ale is a kind of beer
TT stands for teetotal, someone who abstains from alcohol

explanation.surface: A better ale, now being sampled by someone who doesn't drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucked into' suggests eating; here the ale has the teetotaller put inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Better can mean improved, as when someone is recovering from illness.

clue.text: African tree developed with rain

indicators.note: the letters are developed, worked into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree in Africa has grown with the help of rainfall.
explanation.definitionFit: An Eritrean is a person from Eritrea, a country in north-east Africa.

clue.text: Lampoon leaders of several European nations, dismissing unlikely promises

indicators.note: the leaders of the words are their first letters, taken in turn

parts.words: several European nations, dismissing unlikely promises
parts.note: the six words each give their opening letter

explanation.surface: Mocking the heads of several European countries for brushing off implausible pledges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leaders' looks like politicians, but it means the opening letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A send-up is a parody or satire, the same as a lampoon.

clue.text: Medic with a postgrad degree getting work in theatre

parts.note: Dr is a doctor
taken as written
an MA, Master of Arts, is a postgraduate degree

explanation.surface: A doctor with a master's degree finds employment in an operating theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' points to surgery after 'Medic', but it means the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A drama is a play, a work performed on stage.

clue.text: Sign from ladies losing weight

indicators.note: the women lose the letter, so it is taken away

parts.note: ladies are women

explanation.surface: An indication that the ladies are slimming.
explanation.definitionFit: An omen is a portent, a sign of what is to come.

clue.text: Spin-off product that is packaged in metal

indicators.note: these letters are packaged inside the metal, as if in a tin box

parts.note: tin is a metal
i.e. is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A piece of film merchandise comes wrapped in a tin.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is a book, toy or other item linked commercially to a film or show.

clue.text: Moderate consumed with rage at first

indicators.note: the word for rage comes first, before the word for consumed

parts.note: temper is an outburst of anger
ate means consumed

explanation.surface: A calm person was at first eaten up by fury.
explanation.definitionFit: Temperate means restrained and mild, as moderate does, of climate or behaviour.

clue.text: Monkey in Rwanda's borders and southern California

indicators.note: the borders of the country name are its first and last letters

parts.note: the country name itself, without the possessive

explanation.surface: A primate living on the frontiers of Rwanda and in southern California.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey' looks like the animal, but it means a mischievous child.
explanation.definitionFit: A rascal is a cheeky scamp, and a mischievous child is called a little monkey.

clue.text: Not stable yet, Sudan needs reform

indicators.note: the letters need reforming, putting into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Sudan is still shaky and requires political change.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsteady means wobbly or insecure, lacking firm balance.
